claims.claim: For 0≤q≤n, a graph has a dominating set of exactly q vertices if and only if its domination number γ is at most q.
claims.evidence: If an exact q-set exists then γ≤q. Conversely, a minimum dominating set of size γ≤q can be enlarged by arbitrary unused vertices to size q because every superset of a dominating set remains dominating. This includes q=0 and the empty graph.
claims.search_method: Direct monotonicity proof plus exhaustive graph-and-subset enumeration through five vertices.

claims.claim: Greedy closed-neighborhood coverage has residual r≤n(1-1/q)^q whenever γ(G)≤q, for q≥1.
claims.evidence: Extend a minimum dominating set to a q-set D. For every current uncovered set U, the q sets N[d]∩U cover U, so one has size at least |U|/q. Greedy gains at least that much, giving |U_i|≤(1-1/q)|U_{i-1}| and hence the claimed bound after q selections. The checker tested the equivalent integer inequality r q^q≤n(q-1)^q.
claims.search_method: Averaging proof over a q-vertex dominating set plus exact exhaustive checking.

claims.claim: For arbitrary fixed c, greedy gives an exact polynomial-time triage: it solves the instance whenever r≤n/c or r>n(1-1/q)^q.
claims.evidence: For q≥1 and r≤n/c, every residual vertex is outside and nonadjacent to the selected q-set; adding one edge from a selected vertex to each residual vertex uses exactly r edits and makes that set dominate. If r exceeds the theoretical bound, Claim 1's contrapositive gives γ(G)>q, so (G,nil) is correct. All comparisons with the theoretical bound use integers. The q=0 case is separately trivial.
claims.search_method: Constructive repair and contrapositive proof, with exact rational-budget tests on every enumerated graph.

claims.claim: Sidestep(Dominating Set,dist_e,n/c) is in FP for every fixed c≤e.
claims.evidence: For q≥1, either the residual violates Claim 1's exactly testable bound, yielding a correct nil on G, or it can be repaired using r≤n(1-1/q)^q≤n/e≤n/c edits. The exponential inequality follows from ln(1-x)≤-x, with q=1 immediate. For q=0, nil is correct when n>0 and the empty set is correct when n=0. The algorithm is polynomial-time.
claims.search_method: Complete case analysis and analytic inequality, with exhaustive verification of the greedy and repair components.

claims.claim: For every c, all instances with q≥1 and n-q≤n/c have a direct polynomial-time YES output.
claims.evidence: Choose any q-set S and a fixed s∈S. For every vertex outside S not already dominated by S, add its edge to s. These edges were absent, their number is at most n-q≤n/c, and S is then an exact q-vertex dominating set.
claims.search_method: Direct construction plus exhaustive checking for multiple exact rational values of c.

claims.claim: For every c, a computable sparse NO certificate is available when q+1 vertices have at most n/c incident edges in total.
claims.evidence: Given such a vertex set X, delete the distinct edges incident with X. This is computable, uses at most n/c edits, and isolates all q+1 vertices. Every dominating set of the resulting graph must contain X, so no q-set exists. Choosing the q+1 smallest-degree vertices gives the stated polynomially recognizable sufficient subcase because the number of distinct incident edges is at most their degree sum.
claims.search_method: Direct certificate proof plus exhaustive enumeration of every candidate X and several rational edit budgets.

claims.claim: Domination number is one-Lipschitz per edge edit, with a constructive transfer.
claims.evidence: If S dominates H, let U be the vertices not dominated by S in G. Each u∈U uses a distinct edge from E(H)\E(G) to be dominated in H, so |U|≤|E(H)\E(G)|, and S∪U dominates G. Applying this in both directions gives |γ(G)-γ(H)|≤|E(G)△E(H)| and supplies the constructive transfer.
claims.search_method: Bidirectional transfer proof plus exhaustive one-edge and all-dominating-subset checks.

claims.claim: A radius-R sidestep solver decides every additive-gap instance whose YES case has γ(G)≤q-R and whose NO case has γ(G)>q+R.
claims.evidence: For every H at distance at most R, Lipschitzness gives γ(H)≤γ(G)+R≤q in the YES case and γ(H)≥γ(G)-R>q in the NO case. Thus every permitted H has the same answer type, so the solver's set-versus-nil output decides the promise instance.
claims.search_method: Application of the Lipschitz inequality plus exhaustive radius-zero, one, and two balls.

claims.claim: Any FP solver at fixed c yields a polynomial-time additive-2⌊n/c⌋ approximation for Minimum Dominating Set.
claims.evidence: Let R=⌊n/c⌋ and query all q. At q0=min(n,γ(G)+R), every returned graph H within the radius satisfies γ(H)≤γ(G)+R, so some YES occurs by q0. For the least YES q*, transfer its exact q*-set from H to G using Claim 6, adding at most R vertices. The resulting set has size at most q*+R≤γ(G)+2R. There are only n+1 polynomial-time calls.
claims.search_method: Worst-case solver-output argument plus exhaustive transfer and radius-ball checking.

claims.claim: On graphs of maximum degree Δ, the preceding algorithm is a (1+2(Δ+1)/c)-approximation.
claims.evidence: A dominator covers at most Δ+1 vertices, so n≤(Δ+1)γ(G). Claim 8 therefore yields |S|≤γ(G)+2n/c≤(1+2(Δ+1)/c)γ(G). The empty graph is handled trivially.
claims.search_method: Closed-neighborhood counting proof plus exact checking of n≤(Δ+1)γ on all enumerated graphs.

claims.claim: There is an exact approximation-preserving reduction from isolate-free Vertex Cover of maximum degree three to Dominating Set of maximum degree six.
claims.evidence: For each edge uv retain uv and add x_uv adjacent to u and v. A vertex cover dominates the gadget because isolate-freeness ensures every uncovered original vertex has a covered neighbor. Conversely, if a gadget dominating set contains x_uv, replace it by an endpoint; every unselected x_uv was already dominated by an endpoint. The resulting original-vertex set covers every edge and is no larger. Hence γ=τ exactly. Original degrees double and are at most six; new vertices have degree two.
claims.search_method: Two-way solution mapping proof plus exhaustive objective and mapping checks on 558 eligible labeled base graphs.

claims.claim: The universal target implies a PTAS family for cubic Minimum Vertex Cover.
claims.evidence: For fixed ε>0 choose c=14/ε. Apply Claim 8 to the degree-six gadget. Claim 9 gives a (1+14/c)=(1+ε) dominating set; Claim 10 converts it to a no-larger vertex cover while preserving the optimum. Isolated input vertices can be discarded. Runtime is polynomial for every fixed ε, yielding the asserted family.
claims.search_method: Composition of the additive approximation, degree-six ratio, and exact gadget mapping; gadget components were exhaustively checked.

claims.claim: Conditional on the standard APX-hardness theorem for cubic Vertex Cover, the universal target holds if and only if P=NP.
claims.evidence: Under the stated hardness premise, a PTAS—or just the sufficiently accurate fixed-factor algorithm obtained by choosing large enough c—implies P=NP, so Claim 11 proves the forward implication. If P=NP, Dominating Set decision and witness recovery are polynomial-time; output H=G, extend a found set to exactly q, or correctly output nil. This uses zero edits for every c, proving the reverse implication.
claims.search_method: Direct proof of both logical implications, treating the expressly named APX-hardness theorem as the claim's premise.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for an unconditional proof or disproof for every fixed c>0. The draft establishes the full algorithm only for c≤e, gives correct additional cases for arbitrary c, and proves—conditional on the stated standard cubic-Vertex-Cover hardness theorem—that the universal assertion is equivalent to P=NP. Because it neither supplies algorithms for all c>e nor unconditionally rules them out, it does not fully resolve the requested target. These are nevertheless material, correct advances, and the final writeup explicitly says that no unconditional all-c resolution is claimed. Therefore target coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS and the draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is ACCURATE.
